about: The solid-rocket-motor simulation track. Rows are simulation steps, in build order, for the solid booster in Cosmos (C++ and Rust twins; SIMULATION-READING-PLAN.md Phases 8-9). status is built, next or later; built rows describe what the code on master already does. Each reference is a section id in the reading-room contents of that book, or a printed page that resolves to the section containing it. The read note gives the order across books. An empty list means the book does not treat the step.

topics.topic: Chamber state: T₀, 𝓜, γ and c*
topics.build: CombustionProducts takes T₀, 𝓜, γ as inputs and gives c*, C_F. A Cantera equilibrium with condensed Al₂O₃ would compute them.
topics.read: Turns Ch. 2 is the cleanest derivation of adiabatic flame temperature and equilibrium products. Sutton Ch. 5 and Humble Ch. 4 apply it to propellants. Williams §4.2.2 gives I_sp from the reacting nozzle equations. Read Turns → Sutton → Humble → Williams.

topics.topic: Burning rate r = a pⁿ and temperature sensitivity
topics.build: Both temperature laws: Sutton (12-12), and Williams (7-41) on p. 250.
topics.read: Sutton §12.1 and Humble §6.4.5 give the law and the measured (a, n). Williams Ch. 7 explains it: §7.1 the deflagration wave, §7.5 why gas-phase control gives n < 1, §7.6 Eq. (7-41), §7.7 how AP composites burn. Read Sutton → Humble → Williams 7.1, 7.5, 7.6, 7.7. Turns has no propellant burning.

topics.topic: Lumped internal ballistics: the chamber ODE
topics.build: Conservative (y, m_c) state with RK4 that lands exactly on burnout; equilibrium p and the n < 1 stability proof are in solid-ballistics.tex.
topics.read: H&P §12.7 derives the chamber-pressure ODE and its stability. Humble §6.5.1 is the same model as a design procedure. Turns §6 well-stirred reactor is the open control-volume balance with the reaction turned off. Read H&P → Humble → Sutton §12.2 → Turns §6.

topics.topic: Solid gas generator → plenum → N pintle valves
topics.build: Gas-generator mode. Closed-loop valve or pressure control is still open.
topics.read: Huzel p. 116 is the cartridge used as the test case. Turns §6 gives the plenum balance. Sutton §12.5 covers solid-propellant attitude control and side thrusters.

topics.topic: Grain burn-back: A_b(y) and V(y) for star and finocyl grains
topics.build: Analytic star-grain A_b(y) first, then level-set or fast marching for arbitrary 2-D ports. Only tubular and end-burning grains exist now.
topics.read: Sutton §12.3 has the grain shapes and their thrust-curve families. Humble p. 332 has the approximate burning-surface formulas, and §6.3.1 does propellant-mass sizing. Neither combustion book covers geometry.

topics.topic: Golden vector: the Humble §6.6 case study
topics.build: Reproduce §6.6.6–6.6.7: pressure and thrust curves from the preliminary ballistics. This is milestone M7.
topics.read: Read §6.6 straight through after steps 3 and 5. Its inputs come from §6.3 sizing.

topics.topic: Quasi-1-D port flow and erosive burning
topics.build: An axial march with mass addition, per Humble §6.5.2. Erosive burning is local, from Sutton (12-17) or Williams (45)–(46); it replaces the lumped aft-end bound. This is milestone M8.
topics.read: H&P §3.4–3.5 derive the 1-D flow with mass and heat addition. H&P §12.7 gives the port pressure drop and its choking limit. Humble §6.5.2 is the station-by-station march. Williams §7.8 covers the erosive-burning correlations and their threshold. Read H&P 3.4 → H&P 12.7 → Humble 6.5.2 → Sutton 12.1 (erosive part) → Williams 7.8.

topics.topic: Nozzle: two-phase (Al₂O₃) loss and throat erosion
topics.build: Two-phase and throat-erosion corrections to C_F and A_t(t).
topics.read: Sutton §3.5 covers multiphase nozzle flow and §15.2 throat erosion. Williams §4.2.6 is the two-phase theory. Humble §6.3.7 is the sizing view. Turns §10 d² law is the first model for aluminium-droplet burning time; Turns does not cover aluminium itself.

topics.topic: Ignition transient, chuffing and L* (bulk-mode) instability
topics.build: Ignition transient from the full pressure ODE with an igniter mass source. Add a burning-rate lag to show the L* instability.
topics.read: Sutton §14.2–14.3 cover ignition and extinction. Humble §6.3.5 sizes the igniter. Williams §9.4 is the bulk-mode (Helmholtz) oscillation, which is the one the lumped ODE can show, and §9.2 covers intrinsic oscillations and chuffing. Read Sutton → Humble → Williams 9.4 → 9.2.

topics.build: Chamber acoustic modes with a pressure-coupled response function, and particle damping.
topics.read: Sutton §14.4 is the engineering account. H&P §12.8 is the derivation. Williams §9.1 covers modes, admittance, damping (particle damping §9.1.4.7) and combustion response (§9.1.5.4). Read Sutton → H&P → Williams 9.1.
